candidates.title: Euroseas seals bumper charter and $26m boxship sale
candidates.excerpt: Nasdaq-listed Greek containership owner Euroseas has secured a $62,500-a-day charter for a 25-year-old feeder vessel while agreeing to sell its sistership for $26m, capitalising on continued strength in the smaller boxship market. The Aristides Pittas-led company said its 2001-built, 2,556 teu EM Corfu has been fixed for a minimum of 12 and maximum of 14 months at the charterer’s option. The new contract will begin in mid-December, following a scheduled drydocking, and represents a sharp increase from the vessel’s previous employment at $28,000 per day. Euroseas expects the minimum charter period to generate approximately $17.8m in EBITDA. The company has also agreed to sell the 2001-built, 2,556 teu Evridiki G to an unrelated third party for approximately $26m. The vessel is expected to change hands at the end of October, once its current charter expires. Euroseas anticipates recording an accounting gain of approximately $22.5m from the disposal. candidates.title: MSC and HMM send boxship orderbook to new peak
candidates.excerpt: MSC and HMM send boxship orderbook to new peak A flurry of new vessel orders by MSC and HMM has sent the container ship orderbook to new highs as demolition rates remain at basement levels. A further 28 container ships of more than 13,000 teu have boosted the post-2009 orderbook to a new high of 16.2m teu, 46.5% of the current fleet. An order for 20 ships of 24,000 teu by MSC at Hengli Heavy Industries in Dalian has taken the company’s orderbook for ships over 20,000 teu to 62 vessels. South Korean operator HMM has also penned an eight-ship order, worth around $1.5bn, with Hyundai Heavy Industries and HD Hyundai Samho for 13,000 teu LNG dual-fuel units. The newbuildings will be deployed on HMM’s Far East-India-Mediterranean service, said the company.
